transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. I'm here to help. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with really severe mood swings for the past several months. I seem to alternate between periods of feeling extremely high and energetic, and times when I feel deeply depressed and down. It has just been really difficult to manage these constant ups and downs.
During those periods where you feel extremely high or energetic, have you ever experienced things that others couldn't see or hear, or felt that you had special powers or abilities?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I have never seen or heard things that other people couldn't, and I've never felt like I had any special powers.
During those high periods, have these symptoms ever been severe enough to cause significant problems at work or in your relationships, or required you to be hospitalized?
No, I don't think it has ever been severe enough to cause extreme crises or require hospitalization. While those times are definitely difficult to manage, I've still been able to get by.
During the periods when you feel deeply depressed, have you experienced symptoms like significant changes in your sleep or appetite, or a loss of interest in activities you usually enjoy?
Yes, I have definitely lost interest in the activities and hobbies I used to love doing. However, I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my sleep or my appetite during those times.
During those high, energetic periods, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual, talk faster than normal, or find yourself becoming more easily distracted or involved in many new projects?

During those times, I definitely find myself starting multiple activities and getting involved in lots of new projects because I have so much overflowing energy. However, I haven't really noticed needing less sleep, talking faster, or being easily distracted.
How long do these periods of high energy and starting new projects typically last, and how long do your periods of feeling deeply depressed usually last?
The periods where I have high energy and start new projects usually last for about nine months. When I swing into those deeply depressed periods, they tend to last for around eight months.
During the last several years, have you had any periods of two months or longer where your mood was relatively stable, or have you been experiencing these mood swings almost constantly?
I'm not really sure about the last few years, but I haven't noticed any long stable periods recently. It feels like I've just been going back and forth between these moods almost constantly.
During those high energy periods, do you feel an unusually elevated or irritable mood that is clearly different from your normal self, even if you don't feel the need for less sleep?

Yes, during those high-energy times, I feel an incredibly elevated, euphoric mood, but I also get extremely irritable and angry over minor things. These moods shift unpredictably and feel completely different from who I normally am.

Over the past two years, would you say that you have experienced these periods of elevated mood and low mood at least half of the time, without ever having a period of two months where you felt like your usual self?

I'm honestly not quite sure about the exact timeline over the last two years. I can't really recall if there was a full two-month stretch where I felt completely like my usual self, as everything has felt so jumbled up lately.
During these high-energy periods lasting several months, would you say your mood is elevated or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least four consecutive days?

Yes, during those nine-month periods, my mood is abnormally elevated or highly irritable almost every single day, well beyond just four days. I experience rapid shifts where I alternate between feeling extremely happy and euphoric, and getting easily angered by minor things. It feels like a constant roller coaster during those months.

latest_inference.note: The patient describes long-standing, chronic mood instability. While the symptoms of elevated/irritable mood and energy (lasting months) might suggest a Bipolar spectrum disorder, the lack of decreased need for sleep and the chronic, near-constant nature of the cycling (without clear periods of euthymia) warrant keeping both Bipolar II (which requires hypomanic episodes) and Persistent Depressive Disorder (which encompasses chronic dysthymia) in the differential. I need to clarify the intensity and duration of specific diagnostic criteria for hypomania vs. chronic depressive symptoms.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports distinct periods of elevated/irritable mood (hypomania) lasting several months, alternating with periods of depression characterized by anhedonia. The hypomanic episodes do not meet the criteria for mania (no hospitalization or severe functional impairment) and the depressive episodes meet the criteria for a major depressive episode, consistent with Bipolar II Disorder.
